title: Websites Charge iPhone Users 30% More — Legally
hook: If you shopped online today on your iPhone, you might've paid 30% more than the person next to you — for the exact same item.
angle: Dynamic pricing algorithms profile users by device type, browsing history, and location to charge different people different prices — and most consumers have no idea it's happening
audience: Anyone who shops online, especially Apple device users and frequent online shoppers
key_numbers: Amazon changes prices 2.5 million times per day
Mac and iPhone users shown prices up to 30% higher on hotels and flights
Orbitz caught hiding cheaper hotel rooms from Apple users — 2012 WSJ investigation
Repeat visits to a product page can trigger a 15% markup
Incognito browsing saves shoppers $200 to $800 per year
